landmarks.name: George Vari Engineering and Computing Centre
Kerr Hall North
facts: Its four wings form a hollow square around a quad, on the site of the old Toronto Normal School.
It was completed in 1963, the first building built specifically for the institute.

landmarks.name: Library Building
facts: It opened in 1974 as the Learning Resources Centre.

landmarks.name: Sheldon & Tracy Levy Student Learning Centre
landmarks.wikipedia: Sheldon & Tracy Levy Student Learning Centre
facts: It stands at the corner of Yonge Street and Gould Street.
It first opened to students on September 1, 2015.

landmarks.name: South Bond Building
facts: It opened in the fall of 2007 after a renovation that kept the original facade.

landmarks.name: The Image Centre
facts: It is a photography museum in a remodelled former warehouse at Gould and Bond.
It officially opened on September 29, 2012, after the university received 292,000 photographs of the Black Star collection.

landmarks.name: Oakham House
facts: It is a Gothic Revival brick house at Church and Gould Streets.
It was built in 1848 as the home of its architect, William Thomas.

landmarks.name: Heaslip House
facts: It is the home of the G. Raymond Chang School of Continuing Education.
A public school stood on the site from at least 1880 until the 1930s.

landmarks.name: Kerr Hall West
facts: Its triple gym was the home court of the Rams basketball and volleyball teams until 2012.

landmarks.name: Daphne Cockwell Health Sciences Complex
facts: It is the university's newest building.

landmarks.name: Student Campus Centre
facts: It holds the offices of the students' union and The Eyeopener student newspaper.
It incorporated an older house when it was built in 2005.

landmarks.name: Pitman Hall
facts: It is a residence with 565 rooms.
It was completed in 1991; before then O'Keefe House was the only residence.

landmarks.name: Sally Horsfall Eaton Centre for Studies in Community Health
